title: Reduce JavaScript and prefetch cost without weakening features
businessContext: The dashboard imports full answers, fixtures, editors and compilers for every challenge into its client bundle.
problemStatement: Design the system for 500 challenge routes; 200 KB compressed initial-route budget; low-end mobile devices. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Preserve practice, search and account isolation.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 500 challenge routes; 200 KB compressed initial-route budget; low-end mobile devices
functional: Preserve practice, search and account isolation.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Keep the full content registry behind server boundaries and pass intentional summary DTOs to client listing controls.

A summary refactor can accidentally remove search fields, progress IDs or badges. Preserve stable IDs and verify search/readiness parity; keep solutions and fixtures out of listing payloads without dropping user-facing functionality.
alternativeApproaches: It is useful diagnostic evidence but has different compilation, HMR and transfer characteristics. Report the environment and compare production builds before asserting user-facing production results.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Compare route bundles before/after in production.
Verify search, bookmarks, scores and all challenge entry points.
Test cache invalidation for changed inputs and missing generated outputs, and profile low-end CPU hydration.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
